sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write in brief about the dot matrix printer.
questions.answer: In a dot matrix printer the print head hits the paper through an ink ribbon and forms characters and images with combinations of dots. It is cheap and versatile, but noisy, slow and of lower print quality. Its speed is measured in characters per second (CPS).

questions.q: Write the steps to create a data source using an Excel worksheet.
questions.answer: (1) Start Excel and open a worksheet. (2) Type the field names in the first row. (3) Type the records from the second row. (4) Save the worksheet; it can be selected through 'Use an existing list'. (5) Or select the data, copy it, paste it into a new Word document as a table and save it.

questions.q: ABC School wants to send annual-day invitations to parents whose names and addresses are in an Excel file. Explain the steps to merge the Excel file with the Word letter.
questions.answer: (1) Type the invitation in Word (main document). (2) Mailings → Start Mail Merge → Letters. (3) Select Recipients → Use Existing List → choose the Excel file and sheet. (4) Insert merge fields (Address Block, Greeting Line or individual fields) where names and addresses should appear. (5) Preview Results to check the letters. (6) Finish & Merge → Print Documents (or Edit Individual Documents).

questions.q: Expand (any three): IP, KBPS, HTTP, CC.
questions.answer: IP — Internet Protocol; KBPS — Kilobits per second; HTTP — Hypertext Transfer Protocol; CC — Carbon Copy.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Differentiate between a web server and a web browser, with an example of each. (b) Explain the role of 'Cc' and 'Bcc' while composing an e-mail.
questions.answer:
(a) A web server is a computer that stores web pages and serves them in response to users' requests, e.g. Apache, IIS. A web browser is the software on the user's computer that requests and displays web pages, e.g. Internet Explorer, Chrome.
(b) Cc (carbon copy) sends a copy to other people; all recipients can see who received it. Bcc (blind carbon copy) also sends a copy, but Bcc addresses are hidden from the To, Cc and other Bcc recipients.
